findings.detail: Telethon runs with a premium user account session and channel edit capability; session/API credential ownership, rotation, revocation, and least-privilege boundaries are not evidenced.
CHANNEL_ID is loaded from local .env and edit mode accepts an arbitrary message id; no immutable channel allowlist, post-origin binding, operator approval, or change policy is enforced in code.

The watcher reacts to every NewMessage and skips only messages already containing any custom emoji entity; there is no durable event receipt, edit idempotency key, retry ledger, or reconciliation of partial edits.
Any existing custom emoji entity suppresses processing, even when the branded sequence is absent or a different custom emoji was applied; this is not a proof of this worker's prior edit.
Identical copies exist under /root, /root/night-dev, and /root/night-audit while the unit executes /root/bot; provenance and deployment binding across copies are not established.
The systemd unit omits User and sandbox controls, so it defaults to root with broad filesystem/network access and restarts indefinitely.
emoji_ids.json is mutable local configuration with no signature, source/license record, expiry, or review binding; changing IDs changes the edit payload.
Only stdout messages are emitted; no structured edit evidence, approval/reason, failure queue, alert, rollback record, or operator surface is present.

knownBlockers: production key registry/trusted time/revocation/replay controls not established
interpretation: This is a read-only inventory and rejection of acceptance. It grants no Telegram, channel-edit, deployment, provider, customer, writer, or production authority. E0.3 remains first unmet and BLOCKED_OWNER; E0.4 remains non-production IN_PROGRESS.
